One country, four flags, and a capital inside someone else's zone. This is how the Allies carved up Germany after 1945.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ After Germany's surrender on 8 May 1945, the US, UK, Soviet Union and France took over governing it. The formal takeover of authority dates to the Berlin Declaration of 5 June 1945.
2/ The map shows the split: Britain took the north-west, the US took the south including Bavaria, France got a slice in the south-west, and the USSR took the east.
3/ Berlin sat deep inside the Soviet zone, yet it was divided into four sectors too, as the inset shows. That geography set up one of the Cold War's biggest standoffs.
4/ The Americans and British merged their zones into the Bizone on 1 January 1947. France's zone joined later, creating what became known as the Trizone.
5/ In June 1948 the Soviets blockaded the western sectors of Berlin. It lasted until May 1949, and the West kept the city supplied by air.
6/ On 23 May 1949 West Germany was founded. The East German state followed on 7 October 1949. One map of zones became two countries for 41 years.
7/ Did the occupation zones make the division of Germany inevitable, or could it have gone another way? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
